title: Unify playback speed: single source of truth
description: The playback speed slider doesn't stick — dragging it causes the value to snap back to 1.0 on the next frame. Root cause is the fragile two-way sync in playback_controls_system (audit Issue 2). sequence_manager.playback_fps (FPS) and ui_state.playback.speed (multiplier) represent the same concept in different units, and the sync heuristic can't tell which side changed. Fix: make ui_state.playback.speed the single source of truth. Have keyboard +/- in handle_playback_input write directly to ui_state.playback.speed instead of sequence_manager.playback_fps. Remove or derive sequence_manager.playback_fps. See docs/audit-visibility-swap-playback.md §4 Issue 2 and §6 Step 2.

title: Unify frame advancement: fix flickering and stutter
description: playback_controls_system overwrites ui_state.current_frame from sequence_manager every frame (audit Issue 3), which can revert frame advances from playback_update_system causing flicker/stutter. Fix: make sequence_manager.current_frame the single source of truth for frame index. All advancement (keyboard, timer, UI buttons) writes directly to sequence_manager. The UI only reads from it for display. See docs/audit-visibility-swap-playback.md §4 Issue 3 and §6 Step 1.

title: Per-directory settings (seaview.toml)
description: Save and load per-directory settings as seaview.toml in the viewed directory. Initial focus: camera position, source coordinates, playback speed, loop toggle. Settings are loaded on startup and saved via UI controls (e.g. Save Camera button).

title: Define Settings struct with TOML serialization
description:
Create a Settings struct in a new settings module (lib/settings.rs):

- camera_position: [f32; 3] (translation)
- camera_rotation: [f32; 4] (quaternion) or [f32; 3] (euler angles - more human-editable)
- source_coordinates: String (yup/zup/fluidx3d)
- playback_speed: f32
- loop_enabled: bool

Use serde + toml crate for serialization. The struct should have sensible defaults via Default trait. Add toml and serde dependencies to Cargo.toml.

title: Load seaview.toml on startup
description:
When seaview opens a directory or file:

1. Resolve the target directory (parent dir if file, dir itself if directory)
2. Check for seaview.toml in that directory
3. Deserialize into Settings struct
4. Insert as a Bevy Resource
5. Apply settings:
   - Camera: set Transform on camera entity
   - Source coords: override CLI default (CLI flag should still win if explicitly set)
   - Playback: set speed and loop on UiState

Precedence: CLI flags > seaview.toml > built-in defaults

title: Save Camera button in UI
description:
Add a Save Camera (💾) button to the playback controls bar:

1. Read current camera Transform (translation + rotation)
2. Load existing seaview.toml if present (preserve other settings)
3. Update camera fields
4. Write back to seaview.toml in the sequence directory
5. Show brief confirmation in UI (e.g. toast/info message)

The button should sit near the existing center-camera (🎯) button. Needs to know the sequence directory path - get from Args resource or SequenceManager.

title: Save playback settings to seaview.toml
description:
Auto-save or manual-save playback settings (speed, loop) to seaview.toml. Options:

- Option A: Save automatically when changed (may be noisy)
- Option B: Save when Save Camera is pressed (bundle with camera save)
- Option C: Separate 'Save Settings' button

Recommendation: Option B - bundle with camera save. The save button becomes 'Save View' and writes camera + playback state together.

title: Environment panel: light intensity and color chooser
Night simulation lighting system
description:
Add a configurable lighting system for simulating night-time viewing conditions with adjustable point lights placed above the scene.

Key features:
- N point lights, adjustable via slider
- Grid-based placement with multiple plane-filling algorithms (selectable via chooser)
- Configurable height above sea level (metres), adjustable via slider
- Configurable light throw angle (downward cone angle)

This is useful for visualising fluid simulations under realistic night-time illumination (e.g. flood lighting, search lights).

title: N point lights with grid placement
description:
Spawn N SpotLight entities in a grid pattern above the scene.

- N adjustable via egui slider (e.g. 1–100)
- Grid layout: distribute lights evenly across the scene bounding box
- Lights should be SpotLights (not PointLights) so we can control the cone angle
- Store as a resource (NightLightingConfig) so it's reactive to slider changes
- Despawn/respawn lights when N changes

title: Plane-filling algorithm chooser for light placement
description:
Implement multiple algorithms for distributing N lights across the scene area, with a dropdown selector in the UI.

Algorithms to consider:
- Uniform grid (rows x cols closest to sqrt(N))
- Hexagonal packing (offset rows for better coverage)
- Poisson disk sampling (random but evenly spaced)
- Single row / single column (for directional setups)

UI: egui ComboBox to select the active algorithm. Lights reposition when algorithm changes.

title: Height above sea level slider
description:
Add an egui slider controlling the Y-position (height) of all night lights.

- Label: 'Height (m)' 
- Range: e.g. 5–500m, logarithmic scale might feel better
- Updates all light Transform.translation.y in real time
- Default to something sensible relative to mesh bounding box (e.g. 2x mesh height)

title: Light throw angle (cone angle) slider
description:
Per-light angle widget for controlling cone/throw angle.

Approach: Bevy built-in gizmos for 3D cone visualisation + egui panel for per-light controls.

Each light gets:
- A 3D cone wireframe gizmo (Gizmos::circle at the base + lines to apex) showing throw coverage
- An egui slider in a lighting panel for its angle (5°–180°)
- Gizmo updates in real time as slider changes

Future: consider transform-gizmo-bevy v0.8.0 (Bevy 0.16 compatible) for drag-to-position lights in the viewport.

No new crate dependencies needed for initial implementation.
